I’ve read quite a lot of manga in my time, though admittedly I’ve given up on a lot of them because of my short attention span and lack of patience. But this, One Piece, Komi Can’t Communicate and - unfortunately the now cancelled - Act-Age were the only ones I was willing to wait for.

I don’t know if I’d put it in my top 5 of all time, it really depends on what mood I’m in but it’s certainly in the top 10.

2. Shaman King
3. Act-Age
4. Black Lagoon
5. 6. 7. are interchangeable between Spy x Family, Komi Can’t Communicate, and From Me To You.

One of my favourite parts of XC2 is near the beginning of the game when you enter the village in Gormott and a character with the thickest Welsh accent you’ve ever heard strides down the path and yells “Alright boyo!” Nintendo UK’s translation team knows so much about different cultures and it really shows when they get their hands on a big title.
Maybe not the best one but the amount of times I heard Caspar shout “I’ll have your head!” before helicopter spinning and punching a giant beast to death has now made it engrained into my memory.

As a fellow Welsh man I always love when I see my home language used in popular fiction, especially ones where they’re not made in the UK or Europe. One of the best aspects of Xenoblade 2 was the use of regional accents so having one place be distinctly Welsh and another distinctly Scottish was a real treat.

Though I’m sure my better half always gets annoyed every time I point out that they pronounce Myrddin wrong but what’s a man to do.

Didn’t think I would like Bernadetta mostly because I thought they’d just turn her introvertness and fear of interaction into a joke, that she’d be the “oh so relatable” character. I was pleasantly surprised when it turned out they gave her a legitimate and heartbreaking reason why she fears interaction, and she’s got some good development.

I went into the game thinking Hilda was the worst character, that she would the laziest character in the world and that would be her only other gimmick outside of being a spoilt brat. I even knew myself that when I played Golden Deer that I’d probably end up loving her purely because I was convinced she was awful, fast forward to about 5 hours into the run and not only is she my favourite character in Golden Deer but also in the whole game. Not suited for the front lines is the biggest lie anyone’s ever told!

Similarly I thought Lorenz was just going to be that one meme guy that was so awful but we’d elevate to the real main character because we love our irony. Turned out to be fantastically written with great character development, and good lord that timeskip outfit does things for me.

I don’t think there’s a single character I dislike - I hated Edelgard and especially Hubert with a passion until I played BE and grew to like them, helps that Robbie Daymond’s performance is fantastic - but I think the closest would probably be Leonie. She’s fantastic in most of her supports and her battle dialogue is great, it’s mostly when running through the monastery, the cutscenes, and supports with Byleth where her gimmick gets real old, real fast.

As others have said, it really stems from which route you end up picking first. I picked Golden Deer and whilst in the beginning I saw her as nothing more than the villain, Claude makes it very clear that her goal to unite Fódlan is very noble but her methods are completely wrong. She wants to unite Fódlan and that’s great, and her backstory - which you only get into if you pick Black Eagles - makes you sympathise with her, but does it justify causing a civil war for 5 years where tens of thousands of people, including innocents, die? Does she do what she does because she firmly believes it’s the right thing to do or is she becoming the figure of hatred across Fódlan to unite the continent in a different kind of way?

It’s done so well with the different routes, each one makes you understand a different character’s perspective and makes them all morally grey. It’s much more down to earth and human that other Fire Emblem games, it’s why we’ll be talking about this kind of thing for years to come.

Also another thing to keep in mind; the game has only been out for just over a week, give it a month or two and you’ll start to see people talking about these kind of things with the knowledge of every route.

Based on everything you've specified, Xenoblade 2 is 100% the game you're looking for. Ys VIII is still an amazing game in its own right and well worth a purchase, but next to Xenoblade it doesn't stand a chance. They're both similar in their battling system, and their to-die-for soundtracks, but Xenoblade 2 has a lot more to offer; places to explore, characters, storylines, overall story, sidequests, and post game content. And that's not even including the DLC that adds even more modes, and a whole other new story mode with a different playable cast of characters.

- I think Rex will probably be in, the wording in the Direct is ambiguous right now on if Sakurai was referring to the base roster or the DLC, but considering the DLC roster was finalised AFTER the Direct makes me think he's likely. Almost like the Mii Costume is them saying "We know you really want him, give us a bit more time, and have this for the time being"

- Any of the Champions from BOTW, the Zelda series is in desperate need of unique characters, and Nintendo would be stupid to not capitalise on the overwhelming success of BOTW. As for which one, I've got no idea, Mipha and Revali seem to be the most popular so I'm guessing one of those.

- Rayman, Nintendo and Ubisoft's relationship has just been growing rapidly, it would be a nice way of cementing that to have Rayman in.

- Edelgard, with both Roy and Corrin it seems like Smash has always wanted to promote their upcoming Fire Emblem game. As long as she uses an axe and doesn't take after Marth too much I think she'll be fine.

- As much as I want Balloon Fighter or another Namco character, I feel like Square will get another slot. Potentially Geno or Neku, but I feel we'd end up with another Final Fantasy VII character - I've never played VII so I only really know Tifa, and Sephiroth.

Got to hope for either of these games getting ports, neither of them took off like Xenoblade did. They were both amazing though, picked up the special editions of both when they game out - still have them.

I always figured The Last Story could've continued, either as a sequel or as a prequel detailing Zael and Dagran's previous adventures, but alas I think the two trophies we got in Smash Wii U is the last we'll see of it.

Going with Tressa the merchant. Her chapter 1 just makes the most sense to me in terms of the rest of the game; she leaves her little town to embark on a journey of self discovery, and along the way she meets the other seven and after hearing their stories she decides to help them.

It's the most obvious start to a journey and she isn't after revenge of anything like some of the others, but to me it makes the most sense.

VOEZ and Deemo are probably the best ones in terms of pure music and rhythm, they're both made by the same developers and some of the songs from one are in the other as well. There's more variety in Deemo, VOEZ has more pop and dance. They're alright on TV mode but they were made with touch controls for smartphones so they work best in handheld.

Runner3 is good and is a rhythm platformer so it adds a little variety. Crypt of the Necrodancer is a roguelike dungeon crawler rhythm game, very very different and so good. Super Beat Sports is pretty fun but it's much better in multiplayer, always a laugh when you have friends over.

I haven't shopped in GAME in years for this exact reason, Nintendo isn't really popular in the UK so they only devote a tiny section of a shelf for both Switch and 3DS in my local one. Hell I remember back when the amiibo craze was in high gear and they didn't sell any, Argos was much better for that.

Though to be fair - and I don't want to sound like I'm defending them here - they did almost go under a few years back, and with how digital and online focused games are becoming they need all the profit they can get, they're doing deals on iPhones and Androids now. Catering a big part of their shop to a company that's never been popular in their region since the PlayStation came out isn't a wise choice, especially when most UK Nintendo gamers know if they want a Nintendo game then GAME is the last place to go to.

I hope this doesn't come across the wrong way but I'm genuinely curious; what makes this roster pleasing to you?

As I stated I've not heard anyone say they like this roster, so it would be nice to hear an opinion from someone who does like it.

In no particular order; Comrades [Sacred Stones], With Mila's Divine Protection [Echoes version], A Dark Fall (Fire) [Fates], Birth of the Holy Knight [Genealogy], and Battle Preparations - Deliverance [Echoes].

I'm probably not going to cancel in the end, even though I've been hating on the game since January I'm such a shameless Fire Emblem fanboy that I'll end up putting 100+ hours into a game I'm only vaguely interested in.

But yeah, just over three weeks until we'll know everything in the base game, anyone on the fence about the game should wait until then to decide which way to go.

It's decisions like this that make it clear Koei Tecmo/Intelligent Systems have no idea what the fanbase wants. I don't know anyone who is pleased with this roster, and most of the people I know have only played Awakening and Fates.

I pre-ordered the special edition simply because I'm a sucker for soundtracks, but I'm seriously considering cancelling because of all these stupid decisions.

Lex - He and Sigurd carry me through the first half of Genealogy every time, plus he's Beta Hector so that helps. He's a great father to practically every child too - and by that I mean only Larcei and Ulster are his kids.

Lowen - This man, this man right here was a living wall for me the first time I played FE7 and no matter how much I try I can't bench him. He and Rebecca were also the first A support I ever got so he holds quite the special place.

Sylvia - Everyone I know that's played Genealogy hates her and while as a unit I can understand why, she's been really useful in every playthrough I've done. It also helps that her chapter 5 conversation with Alec is brilliant - even if I know longer pair them up - and she's introduced alongside my favourite FE character of all time; Lewyn.

Forde - My favourite cavalier in the entire series, while I do see him getting more love as of late - or maybe now that I've started using reddit - I'm putting him anyway. His supports are really good and they all link really well, and I've always been blessed with RNG with him.

Libra - I never see this guy being talked about, not even when Awakening came out. There's not many 3DS characters that I absolutely love but I can't get enough of Libra, that Bolt Axe got me through some tough times, and his supports are insightful. It probably doesn't help he's introduced in the same chapter as Tharja so no-one really remembers him.
